deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It looks like a wrapper or slip, possibly reused, with bibliographic or library-style notes.

(1) Archival markings: 'Math 21' at top left; an old foliation '44h' struck through and replaced by '15'; a circled '15'.

(2) Near the top, rotated text in Gauss's hand: 'J. B. C. ....' and a short abbreviated word pair (perhaps 'Besch... mit...' or a name). There is also an isolated mark 'xf'.

(3) Main ink entry: a flourished capital 'R' with the numbers 4683 (a small '4' beneath or after it) and 6690, plus an abbreviation read as 'Leosp/1cosp'. These are plausibly catalogue, shelf or lending numbers. Then the title 'Rosaura oder das heimliche Gericht des Schicksals', followed by 'L... Pav[?] von Lafontaine'. This is a novel by the popular sentimental novelist August Heinrich Julius Lafontaine (1758–1831).

(4) Pencil entry: 'Agathe oder das Grabgewölbe von Lafontaine', a second novel title attributed to Lafontaine.

(5) Bottom: repeated flourished capital 'L's, apparently pen trials, and a small superscript '3' with an abbreviation ('fin'/'Fin'?).

Interpretation: these are reading or borrowing notes for light fiction, consistent with Gauss's documented habit of borrowing novels. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. The neighbouring pages (combinatorial and arithmetic scratch work, and statistical counts per hundred) are unrelated in content.

'1cosp' is more plausibly read 'Leosp' or a similar abbreviation; the reading is uncertain.
The number near the 'R' is written '4683' with a small '4' beneath it; '6690' sits below or after it. These are likely catalogue or loan numbers, not a fraction 4683/4.
The bottom row is repeated flourished capital 'L's (pen trials) followed by a superscript '3' and an abbreviation like 'fin'.
The rotated text at top reads 'J. B. C. ....' with an abbreviated word pair below it. 'Besch[?] mit[?]' is a guess; it may be a name.
